purpose: The public repository is a generated artifact of this contract and of the private tree. It is never pushed to directly.

authority.refusal: Any file present in the public repository but absent from this contract, or any file whose rendered content differs from its rule, refuses publication. There is no warn mode.

design_note: Visibility and redaction are orthogonal. A path is visible or not; published content is then transformed. Modelling redaction as a status was wrong: 76 of the 105 files holding a private hostname live under crates/, which must be published, and contracts/relay-policy.json is a normative contract that must be published. One status could not express both facts.

path_statuses.public: Published after the redactions below are applied.
path_statuses.exclude: Not present in the public repository. Requires a reason.
path_statuses.temporary: Published for now, after redactions. Requires an explicit removal condition.

path_rules.reason: sovereign host topology, fleet inventory, and private runtime evidence; public projection relies on abstract contracts only

path_rules.until: build prove-workspace and audit ratchets exist as native surfaces; the public README must not name a gate the public CI does not run

path_rules.reason: shell and python crutches, superseded by native surfaces; the residue is inventoried in CRUTCH_INVENTORY_cynic.md
session notes and third-party coursework unrelated to the runtime

operator sovereign space: personal philosophical work in French prose, plus an Obsidian editor configuration. Pre-legislative per spaces/operator/README.md, and deliberately unindexed in contracts/claims.json so it carries no runtime standing.
a public bounty target: contains a mainnet program address and a submission template
a separate Kotlin product, not one of the runtime crates
agent session scratch, not a runtime artefact
live coordination state, changes on every claim
editor and agent tooling configuration, names tools that are not part of the runtime
a failing external audit report: it names the private builder address and the local clone path of an external project, and it records a FAILURE verdict rather than evidence of the runtime
working notes and audit scratch, superseded by the contracts and rewritten when the underlying finding changes
personal career material, unrelated to the runtime and not part of any technical claim

infra_identities.note: example.invalid is reserved by RFC 2606 and never resolves, so a test aimed at real infrastructure fails loudly instead of silently.

measured_occurrences.note: all published crates and contracts protected by automated RFC 2606 domain and private IPv4 redactions

execution_policy.rule: Execution steps are never run locally. AGENTS.md declares the canonical gate an 'admitted build runner only'. A runner-only step with no supplied evidence is UNKNOWN, which neither refuses nor grants publication. A python renderer was written and then removed: it reimplemented a capability the native surface already owns, and a bootstrap that wraps the thing it is meant to prove is a second authority.
execution_policy.owner: cynic dev publish — renders from the committed state and calls BuildRunnerPort for the execution steps. Not yet implemented. The contract is ahead of the code, which is the only reason a contract is worth writing.
execution_policy.cargo_target_dir: outside the rendered tree; build artefacts inside it would be published

steps.expect: the gate named in the public README is the gate the public CI executes

read_back.on_any_failure: Publication is refused and the public repository is left at its previous state.
